stem: Meera buys a packet of table salt from a shop in Jaipur. The label on the packet says '100% pure salt'. Her science teacher explains that in science the word 'pure' has a special meaning. Which statement about the salt in the packet is correct?

options.text: The salt is a pure substance in science because the label says it is pure.
The salt is a pure substance in science only if it contains just one kind of substance with nothing else mixed in it.
The salt cannot be a pure substance in science because it is sold in a shop.
The salt is a pure substance in science because it looks clean and white.

teacher.key_rationale: A scientifically pure substance contains only one substance and cannot be separated into other kinds of matter by physical processes; a consumer label claim of 'pure' (everyday meaning) does not establish this. B states the scientific criterion correctly. A captures the everyday-label misconception, C and D are invalid criteria (source of purchase and appearance).
